summary: Read-only audit complete; nothing implemented. The scope covers all six incidents, setup, lifecycle, diagnostics, leases, and the MCP contract. The tree contradicts three material claims: model selection is now documented, a macOS LaunchAgent runbook exists, and multi-root support already includes the daemon’s working directory. Additional source-confirmed defects include destructive duplicate startup, isolation that overlooks other orchestrators, and an audit sequence that cannot work as documented.
evidence: Verification boundary: Read all eight requested files and traced their route handlers, registry methods, executor construction, persistence, documentation, and relevant tests. No requests were sent to the live daemon. No registration, lease minting, lane creation, restart, installation, or file-writing tests were performed. A pure bootstrap-builder probe reproduced the emitted commands with a dummy token. Local command discovery confirmed orca-mcp is absent and Node resolves through the Codex-managed fnm alias to v24.14.1. Historical process deaths and the reported live-state counts were not independently re-created.

Severity and ranking: P1 means a path can interrupt active work, undermine an execution boundary, lose orchestration coverage, or prevent the core workflow. P2 means a recoverable setup or contract defect. Rankings below reflect consequence and implementation dependencies; they are source findings, not claims that every additional defect occurred today.

1 — P1 — A second daemon can interfere with the first before discovering the occupied port. Evidence: src/server.js:30 constructs the registry before startServer binds at :882; src/registry.js:103 creates directories, restores state, and starts scheduling; src/registry-persistence.js:127 invokes interrupted-lane recovery; src/registry-lifecycle.js:35 can kill persisted executor process groups and :90 invokes it during recovery. There is no preceding exclusive-instance guard. Consequence: following a future 'start Orca' remedy against this same live checkout can reap the first daemon’s workers or rewrite their state before EADDRINUSE. Fix: acquire exclusive ownership of the canonical state directory and successfully reserve the listener before recovery, migrations, or scheduling. A duplicate start must report the existing instance and make no state or process changes. Validate process identity beyond PID before treating a lock as stale.

2 — P1 — Failure 5: the default fence is excessively broad, and explicit roots silently include cwd. Evidence: src/registry-workspaces.js:86 accepts comma/newline-separated roots; :94 always adds process.cwd(); :101 defaults to HOME plus an outside-HOME launch directory. src/server.js:903 only prints a warning when the variable is absent. Consequence: an adopter can authorize work across HOME unintentionally; even an explicit root list is broader than it appears. Fix: missing configuration means setup-required and no new executor launches. Require explicit roots, validate existing absolute real paths, and remove the implicit cwd addition. A deliberate HOME-wide choice requires a recorded workstation acknowledgement and a persistent warning. Reuse the existing multi-root implementation; do not build another root system.

Correction to failure 5: this is a broad default jail, not literally no path enforcement. Registration checks approved roots at src/registry-agents.js:62, and lane workdirs receive lexical and realpath checks at src/registry-workspaces.js:180. The claimed inability to work on Orca itself is contradicted for this checkout: process.cwd() is included even when ORCA_REPO_ROOTS is set, at src/registry-workspaces.js:94. Effective roots are already returned through the authenticated directory-picker path at src/server-routes/misc.js:79 and src/registry-workspaces.js:177. The defects are silent widening, weak default, and poor agent-facing discovery—not missing multi-root capability.

3 — P1 — Managed writers under different orchestrators can collide too. Evidence: src/registry-lane-create.js:184 counts competing writers only when lane.sessionId equals the current orchestrator; src/registry-agents.js:180 permits multiple orchestrator records for one project. The control-update collision check has the same container restriction at src/registry-lane-ops.js:280. Consequence: two orchestrators for the same checkout can each receive a supposedly sole-writer direct lane. Fix: evaluate conflicts across canonical execution directories and repository boundaries, including other orchestrators and queued writers. Apply the same rule when changing permissions and retrying a direct lane. Preserve direct execution for genuine readers and sole writers.

4 — P1 — Failure 4: lifecycle is manual, and transport readiness is mistaken for daemon readiness. Evidence: package.json:33 starts a foreground Node process; src/mcp-server.js:305 answers initialize, ping, and tools/list without contacting the daemon. Its fetch catch at :210 returns only 'Orca tool call failed: <message>'. Consequence: a healthy stdio connection can coexist with a dead or wrongly configured HTTP daemon, and failure supplies no destination or recovery command. Fix: managed macOS lifecycle commands, bounded downstream readiness checks, and structured errors containing the attempted base URL, operation, cause code, and exact recovery command. Do not automatically replay a mutation after a transport timeout: its outcome may be unknown.

Correction to failure 4: Orca already offers docs/macos-launchd-runbook.md:1, linked from docs/tailscale-mobile-access.md:34. Graceful SIGINT/SIGTERM shutdown and child cleanup also exist at src/server.js:917. The runbook is insufficiently integrated and has concrete faults: its wrapper uses PATH-dependent npm at docs/macos-launchd-runbook.md:58, its env example omits roots at :32, and its 'stop' command sends TERM at :151 despite KeepAlive=true at :95. That command permits relaunch. A LaunchAgent starts at user login and ends at logout; it is not availability before login. [Apple launchd documentation](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/MacOSX/Conceptual/BPSystemStartup/Chapters/CreatingLaunchdJobs.html).

5 — P1 — Failure 6: status reports ownership and managed lanes, with no observation of outside work. Evidence: src/registry-agents.js:359 refreshes ownership, lists this container’s lanes, and returns active/stale flags; :265 also updates project.lastActivityAt when the orchestrator is merely touched. There is no project filesystem or external-process observation in this path. Consequence: continuous polling can keep an empty orchestrator active while independently launched agents work in its project. Correction: the response literally reports active ownership, not a 'healthy machine'; the tool’s 'canonical what is happening' description at src/agent-tools/tool-definitions.js:40 overstates its coverage. Fix: separate connection activity, managed execution, and observed project activity; report coverage and uncertainty explicitly, and surface unmanaged-agent candidates using the bounded design below.

6 — P1 — The advertised audit sequence applies its verdict earlier than claimed. Evidence: docs/agent-orchestrator-skill.md:85 and src/agent-tools/role-instructions.js:22 prescribe findings.record followed by accept/request_fix/block. But src/server-routes/lanes.js:232 dispatches findings directly to acceptLaneAudit, requestLaneFix, or blockLaneAudit. An accepted verdict changes lane.state at src/registry-audit.js:353; src/registry-tool-leases.js:21 excludes accepted from subsequent audit.accept calls. Consequence: the first call already accepts the work, and the documented second call receives 409 on the leased path. Fix: document findings.record as a verdict-applying operation and make the normal example a single audit.accept with findings/reviewedFiles, or a single findings.record with its verdict. Do not create an additional record-only workflow merely to preserve incorrect prose.

7 — P2 — Failure 1: Claude registration defaults to directory-local scope in both emitted variants. Evidence: src/mcp-orchestrator-bootstrap.js:104 builds both clients and globalInstall commands without --scope; README.md:77 and AGENTS.md repeat the same omission. Local claude mcp add --help confirms default local. Consequence: registering from Orca’s checkout does not make Orca available in unrelated project directories. Fix: emit 'claude mcp add --scope user orca ...' consistently and identify the registration scope separately from the executable installation method. Diagnose local/project entries that shadow the user entry. [Claude MCP scope documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp#scope-hierarchy-and-precedence).

Codex scope check: the same missing-flag diagnosis does not apply. src/mcp-orchestrator-bootstrap.js:123 uses codex mcp add, and :135 names the default user config. Installed help exposes no equivalent --scope option; official documentation identifies ~/.codex/config.toml as the default, with trusted project overrides also supported. Keep the Codex command syntax and diagnose its effective configuration location, CODEX_HOME, and project overrides. Do not add Claude’s flag to Codex. [OpenAI MCP documentation](https://developers.openai.com/codex/mcp).

8 — P2 — Failure 2: an unusable PATH launcher is emitted unconditionally. Evidence: package.json:4 marks the package private; :29 declares orca-mcp; src/mcp-orchestrator-bootstrap.js:173 emits it regardless of installation. Local discovery returned 'orca-mcp not found'. Correction: :164 already identifies absolute Node plus bridge as primary, and :188 already explains the npm-link prerequisite. The defect is still real: the returned alternative is not executable as presented. Fix: make absolute-launcher clients canonical and remove globalInstall from normal bootstrap output. Keep the package bin for deliberate linking, without presenting linking or unpublished npm installation as required onboarding.

9 — P2 — Failure 3: bootstrap captures a runtime path it does not own. Evidence: src/mcp-orchestrator-bootstrap.js:162 defaults to process.execPath, as does src/registry-tool-leases.js:454; spawned lane bridges also use process.execPath at src/executor/cli-adapter.js:277. The pure builder probe emitted /Users/alexrodriguez/.codex/fnm/node-versions/v24.14.1/installation/bin/node. Correction: this is not a hardcoded version; an explicit nodePath override already exists at src/server-routes/mcp.js:39. Fix: configure and validate a stable, operator-selected Node executable; preserve its chosen alias rather than replacing it with its versioned realpath. Report both paths and runtime ownership. Recommend an independently maintained runtime; permit the Codex-owned alias only with an explicit dependency warning. Do not install or update Node automatically. PATH inspection confirms the selected runtime here, not an exhaustive claim that no other Node exists anywhere on disk.

10 — P1 — Lease expiry and replacement are operationally surprising, and invalid bootstrap input can revoke working access. Evidence: src/registry-tool-leases.js:421 defaults external bootstrap to 12 hours; :124 caps leases at 24 hours; :315 enforces expiry; :335 updates usage without extending expiry. Re-bootstrap replaces active leases for the same actor and scope at :129 and :444. The replacement is created before launcher validation at :437–454, so an invalid nodePath can revoke the old lease before configuration generation throws. Consequence: polling does not prevent expiry, reusing the default actor can disconnect another setup, and a failed bootstrap can invalidate working access. Fix: validate the entire launcher/configuration before credential changes; make replacement explicit and atomic; expose expiry and replacement effects; provide workstation re-mint/revoke commands and an ownership-recovery path. Polling must be described as refreshing orchestrator liveness, never extending token lifetime.

11 — P2 — Failure 6’s model omission has moved from the skill document to the delivered onboarding surface. Correction: docs/agent-orchestrator-skill.md:44 explicitly includes model, and :51 explains CLI --model passthrough and the blank default. src/registry-lane-create.js:85 accepts it and :324 stores it; src/executor/command-builder.js:127, :163, :188, and :195 forward it for the four first-class CLIs. However, initialize’s spawn example at src/agent-tools/role-instructions.js:19 omits model and permissions, while the tool summary at src/agent-tools/tool-definitions.js:60 merely lists model?. Fix: put per-lane model choice, CLI default behavior, permissions, and reasoning effort directly in the spawn schema and initialize guidance, with an executable example. An unsupported model must produce a visible lane failure; malformed values must not silently become the CLI default.

12 — P2 — Tool descriptions are not sufficient to use every tool without source. Evidence: src/mcp-server.js:127 exposes every mutation body as an unstructured object. TOOL_QUERY_PARAMS at :69 omits orchestrator.list’s documented all/projectId filters, so those arguments are silently ignored despite src/agent-tools/tool-definitions.js:30 and src/server-routes/orchestrators.js:31 supporting them. Short descriptions omit required approval, decision, audit, and lifecycle semantics. src/server-routes/orchestrators.js:143 drops createLane’s nextAction; src/server-routes/lanes.js:203 similarly drops retry guidance. Fix: define typed request/query schemas and examples alongside each existing tool, validate their public fields server-side, forward every advertised query, and preserve actionable error fields consistently.

13 — P2 — First-run documentation has several additional executable contradictions. src/mcp-orchestrator-bootstrap.js:190 tells agents to call the removed orchestrator__update. docs/agent-orchestrator-skill.md:75 says over-capacity spawns queue, but src/registry-lane-create.js:142 rejects them. The document says capacity cannot be changed by a tool at :136, but registration accepts it at src/server-routes/orchestrators.js:78. docs/agent-orchestrator-skill.md:71 promises rejection of other worktree modes, while src/registry-lane-config.js:26 silently normalizes them; explicit isolated also degrades to direct for non-git directories at :45. Its idle-timeout zero-disable claim at docs/agent-orchestrator-skill.md:192 is contradicted by the ||900000 fallback at src/registry.js:39. Isolated executors are told to submit and leave at docs/agent-executor-skill.md:58, without explaining that integration requires committed changes at src/registry-lane-ops.js:792. Fix the prose to current behavior immediately; reject invalid isolation requests and correct the zero-disable parser in their owning implementation stages.

14 — P2 — The bare quickstart does not provide the same ownership semantics as a leased connection. Evidence: src/server-routes/orchestrators.js:57 assigns tokenless callers the shared dashboard identity. src/registry-agents.js:134 deliberately excludes that identity from idempotent re-registration. Consequence: following the skill’s repeated-register instruction through README’s tokenless wiring creates additional orchestrator records instead of refreshing one. Fix: make a scoped lease the normal agent setup even for loopback installations; retain tokenless loopback as workstation bootstrap. Do not merge unrelated tokenless callers by actor name.

15 — P2 — Existing health tooling is a phone-access check, not an adopter doctor. Evidence: scripts/operator-status.mjs:22 checks unauthenticated health, :55 requires Tailscale checks, :58 assumes localhost:3000, and :35 still reports sessions. It checks neither leases, roots, MCP registration scope, nor launcher resolution. src/server-routes/misc.js:17 provides liveness, not readiness. Consequence: a local-only adopter can receive irrelevant failures, while a working health response misses the exact setup failures in the brief. Fix: retain the useful private-access checks behind an explicit remote-access mode and add the consolidated doctor described below.

Already good: the core is worth hardening. Loopback binding is the default at src/server.js:27. Tool leases are hashed, role-limited, resource-scoped, and checked server-side at src/registry-tool-leases.js:111 and :296. API-token and paired-operator authority are separated at src/server.js:284; bootstrap specifically requires admin at src/server-routes/mcp.js:28. Registration and executor adapters perform realpath boundary checks. First-class executors reject raw argv at src/registry-lane-create.js:254. These are structural controls, not prompt-only promises.

Already good: process exit is tracked, graceful shutdown stops children, retry/integration/discard refuse live processes, dirty and unmerged work receive protective refusals, and isolated work is deliberately retained. Audit acceptance requires review and URL-targeted work requires an evidence artifact at src/registry-audit.js:333. The repository has focused tests for leases, ownership, filesystem boundaries, worktrees, subprocess lifecycle, and real stdio-to-HTTP flow, including test/mcp-dogfood-flow.test.js:170 and :258. These tests were inspected, not run; artifact existence checks should not be described as proving the quality of the evidence.

Proposed first run — all new commands below are proposed, not currently available: document clone/cd, supported Node and agent-CLI prerequisites, and lockfile-based dependency installation. Use an explicitly selected Node to run an absolute src/cli.js setup entry. Setup records the checkout path, existing state location, loopback host/port, Node launcher, executor binary paths, and explicit repository roots in owner-only local configuration. Generate absolute Orca and MCP launchers outside the checkout, with no PATH requirement. An existing checkout retains its .orca state and artifacts location; setup must not silently relocate or initialize a different store. State/configuration paths must be printed before service installation.

Proposed first run, continued: configure at least one project root and optionally the Orca checkout as another explicit root; select macOS login persistence; start; run doctor; mint a uniquely named client lease using workstation authority; install the Claude user-scope or Codex user configuration; reconnect and verify downstream readiness. The documented agent example must use actual MCP names and body nesting: orchestrator__register({body:{cwd,title}}), retain its id/projectId, then executor__spawn({orchestratorId,body:{title,executorType:'codex',taskPrompt,model:'<model accepted by that CLI>',permissionsProfile:'read-only',approved:true}}). approved:true records authorization already given for that spawn; it is not permission to invent approval. Poll lane__get until the child exits, inspect output, queue audit if needed, and call audit__accept once with reviewedFiles/findings. For isolated writing work, commit only scoped changes, submit, exit, audit, integrate, then resign. A mock walkthrough proves plumbing; an optional real scout proves installed CLI authentication and execution.

Proposed macOS lifecycle: implement run for foreground development; service install/uninstall with a concrete dry-run preview; and start/stop/status/logs commands. start is idempotent and never takes over an unknown listener or state owner. Generate a secret-free LaunchAgent with absolute executable paths, explicit WorkingDirectory, configured executor PATH or absolute binaries, bounded restart behavior, and known log locations. It must invoke the selected runtime directly rather than npm. stop must unload the job so KeepAlive cannot resurrect it, stop scheduling and new mutations, terminate tracked workers through existing cleanup, drain writes, close the listener, and release instance ownership. Restart must disclose running-lane interruption and require an explicit stop-lanes option when work is active. Describe persistence accurately as restart after crashes and start at login, with logout/sleep limitations.

Runtime ownership and launcher design: preserve one absolute-launcher contract across clients. Before managed setup exists, keep the current absolute Node-plus-bridge clients as the canonical documented path. Managed setup may wrap that same pair in a small absolute launcher that checks both files before exec and can print a remedy even when Node is missing. Do not derive a permanent configuration solely from process.execPath. Check executable access, supported Node version, bridge existence, and the installed PTY module under the chosen runtime. If a stable alias changes target, doctor reports the new target and compatibility result; Orca never selects an unrelated runtime silently.

Fence administration: provide roots list/add/remove through the workstation CLI, with explicit repeated root arguments, realpath validation, configuration source, and effective-versus-pending values. Environment overrides must be visible and strictly parsed; an empty or malformed override must not disable diagnostics. Root changes require a controlled restart in this scope because executor adapters snapshot roots at src/registry.js:78 and src/executor/cli-adapter.js:116. Recheck queued work against the effective fence before launch. Show setup-required, broad-HOME acknowledgement, and out-of-fence project warnings in authenticated dashboard/status/bootstrap responses. Agents may inspect their relevant boundary and request an operator change; they cannot widen it. Explicitly adding Orca is the self-development answer after the implicit cwd exception is removed.

Actionable transport error contract: return stable code, message, baseUrl, method/route, transport cause, HTTP status where present, outcome certainty, and remedy. Example after lifecycle support lands: 'ORCA_DAEMON_UNREACHABLE: POST executor.spawn could not reach http://127.0.0.1:3000 (ECONNREFUSED). No listener accepted the connection; Orca may be stopped or this port may be wrong. Run /Users/alexrodriguez/.local/bin/orca doctor; if this is the configured instance, run /Users/alexrodriguez/.local/bin/orca start.' Generate the actual installed paths and configured URL. Distinguish refusal, timeout, DNS, TLS, non-Orca listener, 401 expired/revoked/missing lease, 403 scope denial, and 409 workflow refusal. Timeouts after dispatch must say the mutation may have happened. Apply bounded requests and the same diagnostics to the permission relay, whose fetches currently lack per-request deadlines and swallow polling errors at src/mcp-server.js:245–272.

Doctor design: one read-only command, usable from any cwd, with human output and --json plus success/degraded/failure exit codes. Check configuration and effective daemon identity; listener reachability and readiness; bridge/daemon version compatibility; selected Node and PTY compatibility; selected executor binary resolution under the service environment; lease presence, expiry, revocation and scope; effective roots and whether the requested project is included; and the effective Orca MCP entry for the selected client, including scope, shadowing, executable, and URL. Mark unavailable client inspection as unknown, never passed. Tailscale is checked only when configured or requested. Do not start processes doing agent work, mint credentials, repair configuration, drain events, or touch project files.

Doctor authorization and agent visibility: add a bounded authenticated self-diagnostic HTTP response so a supplied lease can inspect its own validity and permitted context without listing other credentials. Public health remains data-free liveness; detailed roots, paths, state identity, and lease information stay authenticated and scoped. Initialize performs a short downstream probe and places any failure prominently in its instructions while preserving stdio diagnostics; registration/status include readiness, relevant fence information, and lease expiry. Do not interpret MCP ping or tools/list as HTTP readiness. Preserve existing route authorization tests and add the new endpoint to the unauthenticated sweep.

Lease lifecycle: distinguish the 15-minute orchestrator-idle clock, the 12-hour default external credential, the 24-hour cap, and executor-scoped credentials. Document mint, expiry warning, re-mint, explicit replacement, revoke, and takeover beside setup and in initialize/error guidance. Use a unique actor per independent configuration. Validate proposed launcher/config changes before revoking any old lease. Provide an owner-only credential-file reference for managed MCP setup so an operator can replace the token atomically without editing every client configuration; the bridge can reread that file for the next call. No API admin token is handed to the agent, no indefinite automatic lease extension is introduced, and rotation never retries a potentially completed mutation automatically.

Unmanaged-work reporting: retain activeOrchestrator for ownership compatibility, and add explicit managed-lane counts, last managed execution activity, observation timestamp, coverage state, and warnings. At registration establish a bounded project-change baseline; later comparisons report new changes, not existing dirt, and never attribute authorship from git status alone. On macOS, add bounded same-user process metadata inspection for configured agent executables, resolving candidate cwd only for those processes. Exclude tracked lane processes and identifiable orchestrator/bridge ancestry using PID plus start identity. Report remaining matches inside approved project roots as unmanaged-agent candidates, including when they have made no file changes. Never collect prompts, arguments, environments, or transcripts. Unsupported or denied inspection returns coverage:unknown. Candidate processes and unexplained changes raise warnings in status and the dashboard; they do not authorize killing, importing, or assigning those processes to an orchestrator.

Limit of the unmanaged-work guarantee: Orca cannot make launching another program outside Orca structurally impossible while remaining a local harness. It can make its coverage limit explicit and loudly report supported observations. An idle registration alone is informational; an idle registration plus unmanaged-agent candidates is a concrete warning. Filesystem changes alone may be a human editor or build tool. Process wrappers, inaccessible metadata, work outside cwd, and agents that have already exited prevent exhaustive detection. Tests must exercise these unknown and false-positive cases, not certify that 'no candidates' means 'all work is governed'.

Tool-contract changes — all 29 workflow definitions plus permission_prompt: put parameter types, required fields, defaults, bounds, examples, authorization, side effects, valid states, response fields, and recovery behavior beside the existing tool definitions. Keep one source for schemas and generated examples, and keep server validation authoritative. Explain that outer orchestratorId/laneId/projectId route parameters are distinct from body; registration returns ids but does not currently rewrite the bridge’s environment defaults. Query schemas must include orchestrator.list all/projectId, terminal-tail offset/maxBytes, and event.drain limit/type/afterSeq. Preserve role filtering and the distinction between tool advertisement and authorization.

Tool-specific changes, lifecycle and observation: register needs cwd, title/focus refresh, capacity aliases, ownership/takeover conditions, and returned ids; list needs its actual filters and resigned-versus-stale meaning; status needs liveness-versus-coverage and expiry semantics; resign needs reason and what happens to outstanding lanes. spawn needs supported executor types, required title/taskPrompt, model passthrough, per-CLI permission defaults, intelligenceProfile, isolation, capacity refusal, idle policy, evidence fields, and the approved flag. lane.list/get need state, audit state, model, actual workdir/isolation, process liveness, warnings and resultText. terminal.tail needs its 32 KiB default, 128 KiB maximum, byte offsets and nextOffset; terminal.write needs input/raw behavior and process/terminal preconditions. artifacts.list/get need name handling, encoding and the 2 MiB inline limit at src/registry-lane-ops.js:632.

Tool-specific changes, mutations and audit: submit needs summary/changedFiles/handoff, starting/running preconditions, and 'submit then exit'; shutdown needs approval requirements and child-stop semantics; retry needs accepted retry states, live-process refusal and reset effects; delete needs record/worktree destruction and retained-artifact behavior; controls.update needs exact fields, approval, and a warning that changing stored model/permissions does not reconfigure an already running CLI. Prefer refusing launch-setting edits while a child is live instead of displaying them as effective. approval.request needs kind/detail/requestId; approval.respond needs decision=approve|deny and a pending approvalId; approval.list needs pending/decided response semantics. permission_prompt is the Claude runtime callback, with bounded waits and explicit denial reasons.

Tool-specific changes, completion and remaining tools: queue_one needs valid states and alreadyQueued behavior; findings.record must say that it applies accepted/fix_requested/blocked immediately; accept needs findings/reviewedFiles and evidence requirements; request_fix needs findings/nextTask, retry routing and loop-budget behavior; block requires reason. integrate requires an exited, accepted, isolated lane with committed changes, explains conflicts/nothing-to-merge, and states that push requires workstation admin. discard needs approval, live-process and uncommitted/unmerged-work refusals, force and removeBranch effects. emergency_stop must distinguish this orchestrator from admin-only fleet scope. event.drain must prominently disclose consumption and failed-delivery uncertainty. preview.set needs kind values, update-by-id, URL policy and returned authoritative link. Verify these examples through the leased HTTP path, not only direct registry calls.

Documentation changes: README becomes the short complete install → configure roots/runtime → start → doctor → connect → register → model-selected scout → audit path, linking both agent skills and the lifecycle runbook. Update every Claude snippet, including AGENTS.md. Rewrite the launchd runbook around the supported lifecycle commands, retaining a manual troubleshooting appendix. Correct capacity, isolation, idle timeout, audit ordering, commit requirements, tokenless identity, and lease-clock language in the agent skills. Put model choice and coverage limits near the beginning of initialize instructions. Remove dead tool references from bootstrap text. Add executable-example checks rather than another disconnected capability catalog.

Implementation staging and cost assumptions: S = up to one engineering day; M = 1–3 days; L = 3–5 days, including targeted tests and review. These are estimates, not elapsed-time commitments. SAFE means changes can be applied to this checkout while its current daemon runs. STOP means drain or deliberately stop active workers and stop the daemon before applying/activating the stage here. Server modules are generally cached, but future bridges and children load files from this checkout, so a running daemon can otherwise operate with mixed code. Implement and test runtime stages in a separate checkout with disposable state; never point their tests at port 3000 or this checkout’s .orca/artifacts.

Stage 0 — Correct present-tense documentation and existing-tool guidance. Cost S–M. SAFE for documentation and text-only guidance without changing tool names or wire behavior. Fix scope flags, model prominence, existing launchd discovery/stop semantics, audit ordering, capacity, identity and commit requirements. Describe current limitations; do not advertise future commands yet. Acceptance: all documented tool names exist, examples use correct body/id structure, and each behavioral statement maps to a source contract. Extend documentation checks so bootstrap template text and underscored tool names are covered.

Stage 1 — Exclusive startup and shutdown ownership. Cost M. STOP in the live checkout. Implement the instance/state lock, listener conflict handling before recovery, and orderly listener/write/worker teardown. Acceptance: in disposable fixtures a second same-state process and a conflicting-port process fail without changing state or signaling the first process; stale locks and PID reuse fail safely; normal stop and restart retain records and artifacts. Extend test/process-lifecycle-safety.test.js and test/server.test.js. This stage is independently valuable before adding service management.

Stage 2 — Canonical bootstrap and runtime validation. Cost M. STOP for this checkout because bootstrap and newly spawned bridges share these modules. Add Claude user scope, remove the unconditional PATH variant, preserve explicitly selected stable Node paths, validate before lease replacement, remove dead bootstrap instructions, and disclose expiry/replacement. Acceptance: generated commands register under isolated client homes and remain available from two unrelated directories; missing binaries, paths with spaces, malformed paths and Node alias changes have deterministic results; failed bootstrap leaves the previous lease active. Extend test/mcp-orchestrator-bootstrap.test.js and scripts/mcp-cli-handshake-smoke.mjs.

Stage 3 — Explicit fence and workstation configuration. Cost L. STOP. Add the minimal local configuration/CLI needed for explicit multi-root selection, HOME acknowledgement, effective configuration inspection, and queued-work revalidation. Remove implicit cwd authority throughout registry/adapter configuration. Keep existing state locations. Acceptance: unset/empty/invalid roots cannot launch work; two explicit roots including Orca work; siblings, traversal and symlink escapes fail; launch cwd outside the fence gains no authority; existing records remain inspectable. Extend test/registry-agents.test.js, test/registry.test.js and test/executor-workdir-roots.test.js. Fix zero-disable parsing here as part of validated runtime settings.

Stage 4 — macOS daemon lifecycle. Cost L. STOP for initial conversion of this live instance. Build setup-generated absolute launchers and service install/start/stop/status/logs around Stage 1 ownership and Stage 3 configuration. Acceptance: disposable LaunchAgent survives the starting terminal’s exit, restarts after a fixture crash, stays stopped after unload, uses the configured state/runtime/roots, handles an occupied port safely, and passes a manual login-persistence check. Test commands and plist generation with a fake launchctl first; perform service integration only under an isolated test label. Update the runbook in this same stage.

Stage 5 — Doctor, actionable errors, and lease recovery. Cost L. STOP for coordinated daemon/bridge activation. Add the authenticated self-diagnostic response, read-only CLI doctor, startup readiness reporting, bounded shared error handling including the permission relay, and managed credential-file re-mint/revoke support. Acceptance: stopped daemon, wrong port, non-Orca server, timeout, expired/revoked/wrong-scope lease, unavailable CLI, shadowed client entry, malformed fence, missing runtime, and disabled optional Tailscale each receive distinct results and real recovery commands. Prove no credential disclosure and no automatic mutation retry. Extend test/orca-mcp-server.test.js, auth/bootstrap tests and scripts/unauth-sweep-smoke.mjs.
